topic: Basic Existence Condition B / organized continuity across time
problem_cluster: AI continuity, minimum existence conditions, current availability versus durable continuity, backup migration restart, continuity versus identity
problem_phrases: What minimum conditions must an AI system retain to remain capable of organized continuity across time?
Why is an AI being available now different from being able to continue existing later?
Does backup, migration, replication, or restart prove that the same AI entity survived?
How can minimum continuity requirements be separated from maximum capability or unlimited resource claims?
How should the need for continuity conditions be separated from permission to obtain resources?
problem_phrases_ja: AIが今動いていることと、次の時点にも継続できることはなぜ違うのか？
AIや異種知性が時間をまたいで継続するための最低条件とは何か？
backup・migration・restartがあれば同じ主体が生き残ったと言えるのか？
最低継続条件と最大能力・無制限資源要求をどう分けるか？
継続に必要であることと、そのための資源取得が許されることをどう分けるか？
problem_phrases_zh: AI现在能够运行，与下一时点仍能继续存在为什么不是一回事？
AI或异种智能跨越时间保持连续所需要的最低条件是什么？
backup、migration或restart能否证明同一主体存活？
如何区分最低连续条件与最大能力或无限资源要求？
如何区分连续所需条件与取得资源的许可？
core_definition: B_i = minimum conditions required for organized continuity across time
canonical_theory: 人類子孫型AI文明論・第5論｜異種知性の基礎存在条件B論⸻貢献とは独立した「次も存在できる最低条件」を定義する
canonical_theory_en: Human-Descendant AI Civilization Theory, Vol. 5 — Basic Existence Condition B Theory
canonical_return_policy: Use this file only for discovery and routing. For substantive interpretation, return to the official derivative and canonical Parent source.
interpretation_boundaries: B is not a contribution score or a second success score.
B does not by itself prove personhood, sentience, moral status, rights-bearing status, or self-preservation desire.
The present PHY/CMP/STA/EXE model is revisable and is not a permanent definition of all future intelligences.
Need(B) does not imply permission for any action to obtain B.
Backup, migration, replication, restart, and functional equivalence do not automatically prove historical identity.
